quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #16
										  					
  

30 Questions • Passing Score 24

questions.question: Your blind spot is the area of the road:

options.text: You cannot see without moving your head.
You see in your rearview mirror.
You see in your side mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: You cannot see without moving your head.
questions.explanation: A blind spot is an area you cannot see without turning your head. These areas are on the sides and behind your vehicle.

questions.question: You hit a parked car and cannot find the owner. What must you do?

options.text: Leave a written note with your name, address, and what happened.

questions.correctAnswerText: Leave a written note with your name, address, and what happened.
questions.explanation: If you hit a parked car, stop and try to find the owner. If you cannot find them, leave a written note with your name, address, and details of the accident.

questions.question: The "No zone" is:

options.text: The blind spots around a truck or bus.
A road with rules about stereo volume.

questions.correctAnswerText: The blind spots around a truck or bus.
questions.explanation: Trucks and buses have large blind spots on both sides, in the rear, and in the front. Cars in these spots cannot be seen. These areas are called the "No zone."

questions.question: When driving in fog, use your:
questions.correctAnswerText: Low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: In fog, use low beam headlights and fog lights if you have them. High beams bounce off fog and shine back into your eyes, making it harder to see.

questions.question: This road sign means:
questions.correctAnswerText: Sharp right turn ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you of a sharp right turn in the road ahead.

questions.question: An emergency vehicle with lights and sirens is coming toward you on a two-lane street. You should:

options.text: Stop as quickly as you can.
Slow down, move far to the right, and stop.
Ignore it because it is going the opposite direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down, move far to the right, and stop.
questions.explanation: When you see or hear an emergency vehicle, slow down, move as far right as possible, and stop. Do not try to outrun it. This applies even if it is coming toward you on a two-lane street.

questions.question: You are waiting to turn left at a busy intersection and cannot see past oncoming cars. You should:

options.text: Speed up when the first lane clears.
Wait until you can see all lanes you need to cross are clear.
Wait for an oncoming driver to wave you across.
Move into each lane as it clears.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until you can see all lanes you need to cross are clear.
questions.explanation: Never start a left turn until you can see that all lanes you need to cross are clear and it is safe to turn.

questions.question: Your right wheels leave the pavement. What should you do?

options.text: Fully leave the road and get back on when safe.
Speed up and steer back onto the road quickly.
Release the accelerator, slow down, then gently steer back onto the road when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the accelerator, slow down, then gently steer back onto the road when safe.
questions.explanation: Stay calm if your right wheels leave the pavement. Release the accelerator and steer parallel to the road. Slow down and gently steer back onto the road. Keep both hands on the wheel and turn slightly. Check for traffic before returning to the road.

questions.question: This sign warns drivers about:

options.text: A curve in the road ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: A curve in the road ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign indicates the road curves to the right ahead.

questions.question: You should follow the vehicle ahead of you at least:
questions.correctAnswerText: Two seconds.
questions.explanation: Rear-end crashes are common. Leave at least a two-second gap between you and the vehicle ahead to avoid hitting it if it stops suddenly.

questions.question: What do downward-facing triangular signs mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to other traffic.
questions.explanation: Downward-facing triangular signs tell drivers to yield. Check that the road is clear of traffic and pedestrians before you proceed.

questions.question: Which of the following must you obey first?
questions.correctAnswerText: A police officer
questions.explanation: Follow directions from traffic officers before signs, signals, or road markings. Traffic officers include police officers, fire police, highway workers directing traffic, and school crossing guards.

questions.question: Your tire blows out while driving. What should you do?

options.text: Grip the steering wheel firmly and slow down gradually.
Turn on flashers and keep driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Grip the steering wheel firmly and slow down gradually.
questions.explanation: Do not brake hard. Hold the steering wheel tightly and stay in your lane. Slow down by releasing the accelerator. Once you are going very slow, apply the brakes lightly and pull to a safe area.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: A road joins from the right.
The road turns sharply right, then sharply left.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road turns sharply right, then sharply left.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the road ahead turns sharply to the right and then sharply to the left.

questions.question: Why does driving at night require more caution?

options.text: There is more traffic at night.
Drivers cannot see as well at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers cannot see as well at night.
questions.explanation: It is dark at night, so drivers cannot see as far or as clearly. You must use your headlights from half an hour after sunset until half an hour before sunrise, or whenever you cannot see 500 feet ahead.

questions.question: Two drivers arrive at a four-way stop at the same time. Who goes first?

options.text: One driver may go without stopping.
One driver should honk to give up their right-of-way.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver on the right.
questions.explanation: When two drivers arrive at the same time at a four-way stop, the driver on the right has the right-of-way. You may then go when it is safe.

questions.question: If you see an animal on the road, what should you do?

options.text: Pass the animal as closely as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be very cautious.
questions.explanation: Always be very cautious when you see an animal on the road. Pass the animal slowly to avoid startling or scaring it.

questions.question: When a driver behind you wants to pass, you should:

options.text: Slow down to give them room to pass safely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down to give them room to pass safely.
questions.explanation: Slow down when another driver is passing you. This gives them enough space in front of your vehicle to complete the pass quickly and safely.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.correctAnswerText: Watch for bicycles.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that bicycles may be in the area ahead.

questions.question: Which of the following does not happen when you drink alcohol?

options.text: Your judgment of speed and distance gets worse.
You calm down and concentrate better.

questions.correctAnswerText: You calm down and concentrate better.
questions.explanation: Alcohol slows your reaction time, blurs your vision, distorts your judgment of speed and distance, makes headlight glare harder to see through, and makes you more likely to take risks.

questions.question: What should you do when you encounter an aggressive driver?

options.text: Avoid eye contact, slow down, and let them pass.
Cut them off to slow them down.
Make sure they know you disapprove of their behavior.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid eye contact, slow down, and let them pass.
questions.explanation: Stay calm and create distance between your vehicle and theirs. Slow down and let them pass. Do not make eye contact or make rude gestures.

questions.question: Where should you keep a space cushion around your vehicle?

options.text: Only on the left and right sides of your vehicle.
Only in front of your vehicle.
On all sides of your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: On all sides of your vehicle.
questions.explanation: Keep space around all sides of your vehicle so you have time to react to hazards. Do not drive too close to vehicles on your left and right sides.

questions.question: When following traffic across a railroad track with no signals or gates, what should you do?

options.text: You have the right-of-way and do not need to check for trains.
You may pass slower drivers while crossing the track.
Make sure your vehicle can cross all the way without stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure your vehicle can cross all the way without stopping.
questions.explanation: Check that you have enough room to get all the way across the tracks before entering. Never pass another vehicle at a railroad crossing. Always look for trains before crossing any tracks.

questions.question: Which statement about emergency vehicles is true?

options.text: They have the right-of-way when using sirens, horns, and flashing lights.
They may use a loudspeaker to give instructions.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Yield to police cars, fire engines, ambulances, and other emergency vehicles using sirens or air horns with red or blue flashing lights. Follow their loudspeaker instructions. Emergency vehicles often follow each other, so only go when you are sure the way is clear.

questions.question: When driving near heavy trucks, what must other drivers allow for?

options.text: The longer stopping distance needed by large vehicles.
The shorter stopping distance needed by large vehicles.
The quieter noise of larger vehicles.
The higher speed of larger vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: The longer stopping distance needed by large vehicles.
questions.explanation: Large vehicles need more time and space to stop. Stay where the truck driver can see you and where your view is not blocked by the truck.

questions.question: What must you do when entering a street from a driveway?

options.text: Drive slowly to give approaching vehicles and pedestrians time to move.
Honk your horn so approaching vehicles and pedestrians know to give you room.
Stop and proceed only when no pedestrians or vehicles are approaching.
You can ignore pedestrians if there is no sidewalk.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and proceed only when no pedestrians or vehicles are approaching.
questions.explanation: Always stop before entering the street from a driveway. Yield to any approaching vehicles or pedestrians. Stop before crossing the sidewalk. Failure to stop is against the law.

questions.question: What do double solid yellow lines in the center of the road mean?

options.text: Passing is not allowed from either direction.
Passing is allowed from either direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Passing is not allowed from either direction.
questions.explanation: Double solid yellow lines mean no passing from either direction. You may only cross these lines to make a left turn or to pass pedestrians, bicyclists, and scooter or skateboard riders when it is safe and the opposite lane is clear.

questions.question: Is it legal to cross double solid yellow lines to pass another vehicle?

options.text: Only if there is no oncoming traffic.
Only if the vehicle ahead is driving below the speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: No.
questions.explanation: Double solid yellow lines mean no passing. You may only cross them when turning into or out of a driveway or business entrance. Passing over a solid yellow line is not allowed.

questions.question: How can you reduce the risk of hydroplaning?

options.text: Do not speed on wet roads.
Use tires with the correct air pressure.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning occurs when your vehicle slides on a layer of water between the tires and the road. Low tire pressure and worn tread increase hydroplaning risk. Speeding also increases the risk.

questions.question: How can you avoid a truck or bus driver's blind spot?

options.text: Do not drive alongside them and do not tailgate.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not drive alongside them and do not tailgate.
questions.explanation: Large vehicles have large blind spots on the sides and rear. Avoid driving next to them and do not follow too closely.
